title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter VIII, 'Analysis situs', a 1986 manuscript developing a combinatorial, 'tame' plane topology. The ambient object M is a combinatorial space with 0-dimensional elements M_0 (points/vertices) and 1-dimensional elements M_1 (arcs or segments built from flags, Drap*(L), of a configuration L). A partial order ≤ on elements expresses 'lies in the closure of' or 'is contained in'.

Terminology:
- A 'préfigure' is a set P of such elements. A 'figure' is a closed préfigure, i.e. one containing the boundary points of its arcs.
- supp°(P) is the subspace covered by the 'open ambiance' amb°(X) of the elements X of P. For an arc, amb°(X) is the open arc; for a point, it is the point itself.
- The previous page proved that open supports are unchanged when crossings are resolved, giving a 'non-crossing' préfigure (at most 2 arcs at each vertex).

The theorem on this page is a normal form for constructible subspaces S:
1) Every constructible S equals supp°(P) for a 'monadic' préfigure P. A marginal note renames this 'irredondante' (irredundant). For such P, supp°(P) is the disjoint union of the amb°(X), X in P.
2) Canonical description of P from S:
- P_1 = P ∩ M_1 consists of the elements of S that are 1-dimensional and maximal for ≤ in S (maximal arcs).
- P_0 = P ∩ M_0 is the disjoint union of two parts. The first is (∪_{X∈P_1} ∂X) ∩ S, the endpoints of maximal arcs that belong to S. The second is P_0,is, the isolated vertices of P, equivalently the points of S ∩ M_0 that are maximal in S for ≤.
- Hence P is determined by S. The crossed-out uniqueness claim is replaced by 'en particulier P est bien déterminé par S'.
3) Definition: S is called fermé (or 'fini'; the reading is uncertain) if P is closed, i.e. S is the support of a figure.

Purpose: a combinatorial dictionary between constructible subsets of the tame plane/curve setting and irredundant (normalised) préfigures. The next page uses it for an 'autodual' presentation, treating isolated points in duality with adherent points not in the set.

In modern terms: a constructible subset of a 1-dimensional stratified (PL or o-minimal) complex has a canonical coarsest decomposition into maximal open 1-cells and points.
errors: The uniqueness claim is first written, then crossed out and replaced by 'P is determined by S'. Uniqueness genuinely needs the irredundance and non-crossing normalisation from the previous page; without it P is not unique (e.g. an arc can be subdivided at an interior point lying in S). The page states this only implicitly.
The characterisation of P_0 must exclude points of S lying in the interior of a maximal arc; this is implicit in 'maximal for ≤'. Disjointness of the union depends on this.
The name of the property in the last lines ('fini' vs 'fermé') is ambiguous. 'Fermé' matches 'P est fermée'.

ideas.what: Every constructible subset of a 1-dimensional combinatorial/tame space is uniquely the open support of an irredundant préfigure (maximal open arcs plus points), as a disjoint union.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (coarsest) cell decomposition / normal form of a definable subset of dimension ≤1; minimal stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology; in the o-minimal setting, van den Dries and others (1980s–90s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this detail is unpublished

ideas.what: Distinction between préfigures (arbitrary sets of cells) and figures (closed ones); closed constructible sets are exactly supports of figures.
ideas.modern_name: Open versus closed subcomplexes / constructible versus closed unions of strata

ideas.what: Isolated points of the support treated separately, preparing an 'autodual' description (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Duality of constructible sets (complement/closure duality, Verdier-type duality on constructible functions)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but elementary normal-form lemma for 1-dimensional constructible sets in Grothendieck's combinatorial tame-topology setting. Historically it documents his 1986 attempt to build 'analysis situs' from finite combinatorial data, but the mathematics itself is routine and well known in PL/o-minimal form.
transcription_corrections: The marginal note '* je dis plutôt : "irredondante"' is attached to 'monadique' (the asterisk), i.e. it renames monadic préfigures as irredundant ones.
The insertion after 'de dimension 1 et' likely reads '(i.e. pas réduit à un point)' or similar, not 'pas cell[?], cl. point[?]'.
The word 'fini' in 'On dit que S est fini' may be 'fermé', consistent with 'si P est fermée'.
'v.a.' near the end is likely 'i.e.' or 'resp.'; the sentence ends 'si S est le support d'une figure'.
The first union is ⋃ amb°(P) (stated as a union over X∈P), with the crossed-out symbol (X) corrected.
